title: Stats store: fact table DDL and DuckDB views for route ledger facts
body:
## Goal
Create the schema for the granular stats store: `fact_attempt`, `fact_route_decision`, `fact_session`,
`fact_turn`, `fact_tool_call`, `fact_decision` (projection shape), `fact_outcome`, `fact_feedback` (shape),
`fact_link`, and the `v_*` DuckDB views over the Parquet tree.

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Read design §4.2 (schemas, column types), §4.2.5 (contract for code#9373/9374), §4.9 (views used by queries).
V1 facts that constrain types: `quota` JSON has four shapes (design §2 fact 1); `cost_usd` is NULL on 205,231
rows; `provider_id` is not normalised (fact 3); `variant` values include `xhigh`, `max`, `none`, NULL (fact 5).

## Files
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/schema/facts.sql` (new): DDL in DuckDB dialect, one `CREATE TABLE` per fact,
  with `schema_version` on every table.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/schema/views.sql` (new): `read_parquet('…/*/*.parquet', hive_partitioning = true)`
  views `v_attempt`, `v_decision`, `v_session`, `v_turn`, `v_tool_call`, `v_decision_record`,
  `v_outcome_current` (latest `outcome_code` per subject), `v_dim_model_current`, `v_rollup_latest`.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/schema/README.md` (new): grain statement per table (one sentence each).

## Approach
Follow design §4.2 exactly; enums are closed (`CHECK` in DDL). Outcome codes come from design §4.2.2 and are
loaded from one list (`schema/outcome_codes.json`), never typed twice. No table is updated in place; the
`v_outcome_current` view is the only "current" reader.

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `duckdb -c ".read pm-stack/route-ledger-export/schema/facts.sql"` on an empty DB exits 0.
2. `duckdb -c ".read pm-stack/route-ledger-export/schema/views.sql"` on an empty Parquet tree (no files) exits 0
   and each view returns zero rows.
3. Every fact table has `schema_version` and `ingested_at_ms` columns (checked by a test that parses the DDL).
4. Test oracle: the DDL column list equals the column table in design §4.2 (test reads the markdown table and
   compares names; a mismatch fails). Invariant test (PBT, `fast-check` or equivalent): for any generated outcome
   code outside the enum, the insert fails.

## Not in this slice
No data is written. The exporter is D3-S6.

title: Stats store: measure storage growth per table per day
body:
## Goal
Measure, every night, the bytes and rows per table per day, so the retention decision (design §4.6.3) is made on
30 days of data, not on an estimate. Brief §6: "keep full granularity and measure storage growth".

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Measured baseline (design §4.6.1, 2026-11-13): `route_decision` ≈1,350 B/row, 131 k–224 k rows/day → ≈120–300 MB/day
of text; `route_attempt` ≈230 B/row, ≈45 k rows/day → ≈10 MB/day. The baseline estimate understated `route_decision`
by about 10× (design §2 fact 8).

## Files
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/schema/facts.sql`: add `storage_growth` table (D3-S1 DDL file, one new statement).
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/route-ledger-export.mjs`: after each run, write one `storage_growth` row per table
  per UTC day (`rows`, `sqlite_dbstat_bytes` from `dbstat` when available, `parquet_bytes`, `bytes_per_row_raw`,
  `bytes_per_row_parquet`, `export_version`).
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/route-ledger-export.test.mjs`: test for the growth row.

## Approach
Use `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM <t> WHERE time_… >= ? AND time_… < ?` for rows; `dbstat` may be unavailable in a
read-only connection, so it is nullable and the Parquet byte count is the primary measure. Backfill the days
already in the DB (from 2026-10-24 for route tables, 2026-01-18 for session tables) in one pass.

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `bun test pm-stack/route-ledger-export` passes the growth-row test.
2. After one run on the live DB, `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT day) FROM storage_growth WHERE table_name='route_decision'`
   is at least 10 (backfill covered).
3. Test oracle (exact): for a fixture DB with known row counts per day, `rows` equals `COUNT(*)` per day computed
   by a separate `sqlite3` query in the test. Mismatch fails.
4. Report written to the design's §4.6.1 by a follow-up docs edit with the measured bytes/row (not in this slice).

title: Stats store: dimensions, variant rules, crosswalk, rung table, change markers
body:
## Goal
Build the dimension tables the facts join to: `dim_model` (Type 2, lineage, AA version and test date, variant
splits), `dim_model_lineage`, `dim_model_alias` (ledger id → family and variant; the AA name crosswalk),
`dim_model_match` (price / ability / speed targets with provenance), `dim_door` (Type 2), `dim_provider`,
`dim_pool` (Type 2), `dim_effort` (rung table as data, AD1), `dim_time`, `change_marker`, `change_marker_measure`.

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Read: design §4.2.4 (dimension columns), §4.2.3 (tag namespaces), §4.3 (change markers), §6 (variant rules
"Luna 6 and 6.1 fully separate"; DeepSeek variants by the variant each provider serves), §7 Q-D3-1, Q-D3-12, Q-D3-13.
Ledger facts: `provider_id` spellings (baseline/design §2 fact 3); DeepSeek ids (design §2 fact 4);
AA prices: `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/aa-last-good.json` `section.prices` (13 rows, OpenRouter-style names).

## Files
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/dims/*.json` (new, git-tracked, reviewed): `models.json`, `model_alias.json`,
  `lineage.json`, `doors.json`, `providers.json`, `pools.json`, `effort_rungs.json`, `change_markers.json`.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/schema/dims.sql` (new): DDL.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/dims.mjs` (new): loads and validates the JSON (every `model_sk` referenced exists;
  every raw provider id maps; no two `is_current` rows for one model key).

## Approach
- Variant rows: DeepSeek `classic` and `snapshot-1017` (ledger ids) are separate `dim_model` rows under one family;
  `snapshot-1107` is **not** created until the variant is observed (Q-D3-1). Luna 6 (`gpt-6-luna`) and Luna 6.1
  (`gpt-6.1-terra`) are separate families.
- Rung table: `xhigh|max|ultra|fast → high (alias)`, `default → medium (alias, declared)`,
  `none|minimal → low (alias, declared)`; DeepSeek `medium → high` on Go and ClinePass and `low → high` on Pro are
  `declared = true` rows citing their PRs (brief §9).
- The validator fails the build on an unmapped `provider_id` seen in the last 30 days (the exporter reports it
  as `UNMAPPED`; the validator is the gate).

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `python3 -I -m json.tool` (or `bun run dims.mjs --check`) validates all JSON files; exit 0.
2. Test oracle (exact): every distinct `provider_id` in `route_attempt` for the last 30 days (live query, run in
   the test against a copy of the DB, read-only) maps to a `provider_norm`; zero `UNMAPPED`.
3. Test: `dim_model` has exactly one `is_current` row per `(family, variant_key)`; `dim_model_lineage` `seq` is
   contiguous per family (property test over the loaded JSON).
4. Test: no fact of Luna 6 joins to a `model_sk` in the 6.1 family (a fixed pair of ids; exact).

title: Stats store: tool-call facts with mcpx and fleet subcommand parsing
body:
## Goal
Build `fact_tool_call` from `session_message` tool parts, with `mcpx` per namespace/tool (parsed from `mcpx_exec`
TypeScript) and `fleet` per subcommand/action (parsed from `shell` commands). Brief §5: "mcpx and fleet tool usage,
each per subcommand / action".

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §4.2.1 (`fact_tool_call` columns), §4.6.4 (regexes), §4.7 (dependence on code#9373/code#9374).
Measured: tool parts since 2026-11-06 — `shell` 146,683, `execute` 34,143, `read` 19,911, `mcpx_exec` ~600
(baseline S2b); tool part `state.status` ∈ {completed, error, running, streaming}.

## Files
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/tools.mjs` (new): pure functions `parseMcpxCalls(source)` and `parseFleetCommand(cmd)`.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/tools.test.mjs` (new): golden corpus.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/schema/facts.sql`: no change (D3-S1 defines the table).

## Approach
- `parseMcpxCalls`: match `tools\.([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\.([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\(` and the bracket form
  `tools\[\s*"([^"]+)"\s*\]\[\s*"([^"]+)"\s*\]\(`; one row per occurrence, `source = script-parse`.
- `parseFleetCommand`: `\bfleet\s+([a-z][a-z-]*)(?:\s+([a-z][a-z-]*))?` on `state.input.command`; `source` =
  `session-message` with the regex version in the row (`parser_version`).
- Never store tool input or output content, only lengths.

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `bun test pm-stack/route-ledger-export/tools.test.mjs` passes.
2. Golden corpus (checked-in, ≥ 40 real snippets, copied from the live DB with secrets removed): each snippet's
   expected parse is in the corpus file. Exact oracle: parse output equals the golden list.
3. Property test: for any generated script containing `k` calls of the dotted form, the parser returns `k` rows
   (generator emits random namespaces/tools and random whitespace).
4. Guard: a snippet containing `tools.` inside a string literal is documented as a known false positive; the test
   asserts the count so a change is visible.

title: Stats store: move the rollup oracle into the repo and gate it
body:
## Goal
Make `research/prototypes/stats_rollup_oracle.py` the reference oracle for every rollup: copy it into the repo
and run its invariants in CI-on-main style tests. Brief §5 statistics and AD8 "mergeable rollups; quantiles
within α; every quantile with n".

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §3.3 (quantile choice), §4.4 (statistics set and merge classes), §4.10 (oracle as test oracle).
Re-run 2026-11-13 with 20 seeds: PASS; max quantile relative error 0.009997 (bound 0.01); 1,440 of 1,440 day cells
below n = 1,000 (p99.9 unresolved).

## Files
- `scripts/stats/stats_rollup_oracle.py` (new; copied from the prototype, unchanged logic; header states the contract).
- `scripts/stats/test_stats_rollup_oracle.py` (new): runs the oracle for ≥ 200 seeds and asserts exit 0.
- Run as `python3 -I scripts/stats/test_stats_rollup_oracle.py`.

## Approach
Do not change the oracle's maths. The test asserts the four invariants (conservation, exact merge for
count/sum/min/max/mode, float merge within 1e-9 for mean/stddev, sketch quantiles within α) and the mutation check
(removing the Chan cross term must fail). Add a `--mutation` flag that runs the mutation and expects failure.

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `python3 -I scripts/stats/test_stats_rollup_oracle.py --seeds 200` exits 0 and prints PASS.
2. `python3 -I scripts/stats/test_stats_rollup_oracle.py --mutation` exits 0 only if the mutation test fails
   (proves the oracle can detect a broken merge).
3. Test oracle is the oracle itself (it is the reference); the production rollup (D3-S9) must pass the same
   invariants on the same generated events.

title: Stats store: nightly read-only exporter from opencode.db to Parquet by day
body:
## Goal
A laptop systemd timer that reads `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` read-only and writes the fact tables as
Parquet, partitioned by UTC day, with high-water marks, idempotent per day, and a storage_growth row per run.

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §4.6.4 (pipeline steps, paths, partitioning, timer), §3.9 (location choice), §2 (live facts). Precedent:
`pm-stack/cloudflare-export/` (same shape: `.mjs`, `.sh`, `.service`, `.timer`, `install-laptop.sh`, `README.md`).
Reads use `bun:sqlite` with `{ readonly: true }`, as `pm-stack/aggregator/src/analytics-store.ts` does.

## Files (new)
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/route-ledger-export.mjs`
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/route-ledger-export.sh`, `.service`, `.timer` (03:20 CT nightly), `install-laptop.sh`
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/README.md`
- state: `~/.local/state/route-ledger/export-state.json` (not in repo); outputs under `~/.local/state/route-ledger/`.

## Approach
1. Open the DB read-only; never copy the whole file.
2. High-water marks per table (route_attempt.id; route_decision.id; route_health.id; session_v2.time_updated;
   session_message.time_created for assistant/user/idle/compaction types).
3. Batch 50,000 rows; parse quota JSON (four shapes), normalise provider via `dims`, map effort via rung table,
   explode tool parts via D3-S4 `tools.mjs`.
4. Write NDJSON staging per day; convert to Parquet with the DuckDB CLI (`COPY … (FORMAT PARQUET)`); one file per
   table per day, re-running a day replaces its file atomically.
5. Advance the marks only after the Parquet write succeeds (atomic rename of `export-state.json`).
6. DuckDB CLI missing → keep NDJSON, exit non-zero with a clear message (Q-D3-8).

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `bash pm-stack/route-ledger-export/route-ledger-export.sh --dry-run` on the live DB: reports row counts per table
   that equal `sqlite3 -readonly` `COUNT(*)` for the same windows (exact oracle, checked in the test).
2. Idempotence: two consecutive runs produce byte-identical per-day Parquet row counts and an unchanged
   `export-state.json` on the second run.
3. Read-only guard: the test opens the DB with `readonly: true` and asserts that an INSERT throws.
4. `bun test pm-stack/route-ledger-export` passes.
5. Operator script contract (AGENTS.md "Operator script argument contract"): the `.mjs` declares its full
   argument list (`--dry-run`, `--since`, `--tables`) and rejects any unknown flag with a non-zero exit before
   any file write.

title: Stats store: derived cost with provenance and calibration against recorded cost_usd
body:
## Goal
Derive `cost_list_usd` and `cost_paid_usd` per attempt from tokens × AA price table, with `cost_basis`,
`price_version`, and a calibration against the 50,367 recorded `cost_usd > 0` rows. Answers design Q-D3-3
(is `tokens_output` inclusive of reasoning?) with data. Brief §7 "real cost per %-dollar" and "extrapolate
where we differ from AA".

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §4.8.1 (formula and cost_basis rules), §3.6 (cost-basis options), §7 Q-D3-3, Q-D3-13.
Measured: `cost_usd > 0` on 50,367 rows; all have token counts. Price table: 13 rows, OpenRouter-style names.

## Files
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/cost.mjs` (new): `deriveCost(attempt, price, door)` pure function.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/cost.test.mjs` (new).
- `docs/…`: none. Findings go into design §4.8.1 by a docs edit in the same PR.

## Approach
Compute both reasoning conventions (included in output; separate) on the recorded rows; report the match rate
(±1 %) and median absolute error per door for each convention. Pick the convention with the higher match rate,
record it in `dims/` as `reasoning_in_output` with the evidence file path. Report unmatched models (no AA price row)
as a list: that list is the crosswalk backlog (D3-S3).

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `bun test pm-stack/route-ledger-export/cost.test.mjs` passes.
2. Calibration report `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/calibration/cost-2026-11-13.json` contains, per door, `n`,
   `match_rate_1pct`, `median_abs_error` and the convention chosen; the test reads it and asserts `n ≥ 100` per
   reported door.
3. Test oracle: the recorded `cost_usd` (where present) is the reference; a derived value that matches within ±1 %
   counts as a match; no other oracle is used.
4. `cost_basis` is never `derived-aa` for a plan door (exact test over fixture rows).

title: Stats store: time-window join of quota percent onto attempts (inferred)
body:
## Goal
Attach the nearest S4 quota percent reading before and after each attempt for its door's window, flagged
`inferred = true`, with the reading lag recorded. Brief §5 "existing time and quota % per session, task, PR, or
attempt".

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §4.8.2 (join rule, 30-minute window, reset detection), §3.7 (options), §2 fact 10 (S4 keys by
`serviceId`/`metricId`; examples `opencode-go` 5h/weekly/monthly; `openai:codex` weekly; `antigravity` per model).
Source: `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/snapshots/usage-YYYY-MM.jsonl` (fields: `ts`, `serviceId`, `metricId`,
`value`, `unit`, `limit`, `resetsAt`, `source`, `observedBy`).

## Files
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/quota-join.mjs` (new): `joinQuota(attempts, readings, doorMap, {windowMin: 30})`.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/quota-join.test.mjs` (new).
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/dims/doors.json`: add `quota_service` and `quota_metric_map` per door (reviewed).

## Approach
Implement design §4.8.2 exactly. Readings are only used for a door whose `quota_service` is set; unmapped doors get
NULLs, counted. `reset-suspected` when `after < before`, never a negative use.

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `bun test pm-stack/route-ledger-export/quota-join.test.mjs` passes.
2. Exact oracle (fixture): a hand-built set of 5 attempts and 8 readings with known nearest-prior/nearest-after
   values; the join output equals the expected table (test asserts every field).
3. Property test: for any attempt time `t` and readings sorted by `ts`, the chosen `before` reading has the maximal
   `ts ≤ t` among readings within the window (generator-based).
4. Every output row has `quota_pct_source = 'snapshot-window-join'` and `inferred = true` (exact check).

title: Stats store: production rollups as mergeable states and stat_rollup_event
body:
## Goal
The production rollup: per group and window, mergeable states (count, sum, min, max, Welford mean/M2 with Chan
merge, DDSketch α = 1 % histogram, exact value map for discrete fields), and an append-only `stat_rollup_event`
row per generated rollup (generation time, generator version, AA version and test date, time-frame basis,
counts of sessions/turns/tokens, models/efforts/providers/pools/doors covered, state digest, input membership).

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §4.4 (statistics set, merge classes, reporting rules), §4.5 (aggregates as events), §4.6.3 (rollup tiers and
the three clocks), §3.3 (quantile method, nearest rank).

## Files
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/rollup.mjs` (new): state merge and finalisation.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/rollup.test.mjs` (new): runs the oracle invariants on generated events.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/schema/facts.sql`: `stat_rollup_event` DDL (one statement, append-only).

## Approach
Implement the same nearest-rank definition as the oracle (`ceil(q·n)`), the same α, the same Chan formula. Store
`quantile_method = nearest_rank_v1`, `alpha`. Every output row carries `n` for each quantile and the `unresolved`
flag where n is below the threshold (design Q-D3-4 defaults: p90 ≥ 100, p99.9 ≥ 1000).

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `python3 -I scripts/stats/test_stats_rollup_oracle.py --seeds 200` (D3-S5) passes, and
   `bun test pm-stack/route-ledger-export/rollup.test.mjs` runs the same invariants on JS-generated events and passes.
2. Cross-implementation oracle: for one fixed seed the JS rollup and the Python oracle produce the same exact fields
   (count, sum, min, max, mode, mode±x) and the quantiles within α.
3. `stat_rollup_event` is append-only: test attempts an UPDATE and a DELETE and asserts both are rejected by the
   writer (exact).
4. Re-running the same window with the same inputs produces the same `rollup_id` and `state_digest` (idempotence).

title: Stats store: data-basis query set, one SQL file per brief §5 dimension
body:
## Goal
Put the data-basis queries for D1 and D4 into `scripts/stats/queries/`, one file per dimension, each with a header
(dimension, source, oracle, status). Run in SQLite read-only against the live DB now; the same logic runs on the
`v_*` views after D3-S6.

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §4.9 (the query table, Q01–Q16, status T/D, live results). The queries below were run read-only on
2026-11-13. Parameter `:since` is epoch ms.

## Files (new)
- `scripts/stats/queries/q01_target_effort_success.sql` … `q16_ttft_step.sql` (one per row of design §4.9 table).
- `scripts/stats/queries/run_queries.sh`: runs each file with `sqlite3 -readonly -cmd ".parameter set :since …"`.
- `scripts/stats/queries/README.md`: the table of dimensions → files.

## Queries (T = run and checked 2026-11-13)

Q01 (target, effort: attempts and success):
```sql
SELECT route_id, provider_id, model_id, COALESCE(variant,'-') AS variant,
       COUNT(*) AS attempts, SUM(outcome = 'success') AS ok,
       ROUND(1.0 * SUM(outcome = 'success') / COUNT(*), 4) AS success_rate
FROM route_attempt WHERE time_started >= :since
GROUP BY route_id, provider_id, model_id, variant ORDER BY attempts DESC;
```

Q02 (pool offered vs chosen):
```sql
SELECT route_id, j.value AS candidate, COUNT(*) AS offered, SUM(chosen = j.value) AS chosen
FROM route_decision, json_each(candidates) j WHERE time >= :since
GROUP BY route_id, candidate ORDER BY offered DESC;
```

Q04 (sub-session count and depth):
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE t(root, id, depth) AS (
  SELECT id, id, 0 FROM session_v2 WHERE parent_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT t.root, s.id, t.depth + 1 FROM session_v2 s JOIN t ON s.parent_id = t.id)
SELECT root, MAX(depth) AS max_depth, COUNT(*) - 1 AS descendants
FROM t GROUP BY root HAVING MAX(depth) > 0 ORDER BY descendants DESC;
```

Q06 (tool usage by name):
```sql
SELECT json_extract(j.value,'$.name') AS tool, COUNT(*) AS calls
FROM session_message sm, json_each(sm.data,'$.content') j
WHERE sm.type = 'assistant' AND sm.time_created >= :since
  AND json_extract(j.value,'$.type') = 'tool'
GROUP BY tool ORDER BY calls DESC;
```

Q12 (active minutes, 5-minute gap clip):
```sql
WITH a AS (
  SELECT session_id, time_created AS t,
         LAG(time_created) OVER (PARTITION BY session_id ORDER BY time_created) AS prev
  FROM session_message WHERE type = 'assistant' AND time_created >= :since),
g AS (SELECT session_id, MAX(0, t - prev) AS gap FROM a WHERE prev IS NOT NULL)
SELECT session_id,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN gap <= 300000 THEN gap ELSE 0 END) / 60000.0, 2) AS active_minutes_5m
FROM g GROUP BY session_id;
```

Q15 (statistics block, nearest rank):
```sql
WITH s AS (
  SELECT route_id, provider_id, model_id, COALESCE(variant,'-') AS variant, response_ms AS v
  FROM route_attempt WHERE outcome = 'success' AND response_ms IS NOT NULL AND time_started >= :since),
r AS (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY route_id, provider_id, model_id, variant ORDER BY v) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY route_id, provider_id, model_id, variant) AS n
  FROM s)
SELECT route_id, provider_id, model_id, variant, n,
       MIN(v) AS min_v, MAX(v) AS max_v, ROUND(AVG(v), 1) AS mean_v,
       MIN(CASE WHEN rn = MAX(1, (n + 1) / 2) THEN v END) AS p50,
       MIN(CASE WHEN rn = MAX(1, (3*n + 3) / 4) THEN v END) AS q3,
       MIN(CASE WHEN rn = MAX(1, (9*n + 9) / 10) THEN v END) AS p90,
       MIN(CASE WHEN rn = MAX(1, (99*n + 99) / 100) THEN v END) AS p99
FROM r GROUP BY route_id, provider_id, model_id, variant, n HAVING n >= 30 ORDER BY n DESC;
```

Q16 (TTFT proxy and step time):
```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS turns,
       AVG(json_extract(data,'$.time.streamed') - json_extract(data,'$.time.created'))  AS ttft_proxy_ms_mean,
       AVG(json_extract(data,'$.time.completed') - json_extract(data,'$.time.created')) AS step_ms_mean
FROM session_message WHERE type = 'assistant' AND time_created >= :since
  AND json_extract(data,'$.time.streamed') IS NOT NULL;
```

Q03, Q05, Q09, Q10, Q11, Q13 are one-line aggregates over `session_v2` / `route_attempt` / `route_decision`; their
text is in design §4.9. Q07, Q08 run over `v_tool_call` (D3-S4) and Q14 over `v_attempt` + `v_quota_reading` (D3-S8).

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `bash scripts/stats/queries/run_queries.sh --since 2026-11-06` exits 0 on the live DB (read-only) and prints
   one block per file.
2. Oracle (exact): for Q15 the number of rows with `n >= 30` equals the same count computed in Python from a
   `sqlite3 -readonly` dump of the same window; the p50/p90/p99 values equal the Python nearest-rank values exactly.
3. Oracle (exact): Q04 counts sum to `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session_v2` for the roots + descendants walk (equal to
   the total, so no session is unreachable at query time; a mismatch names the orphan ids).
4. No file uses `SELECT *` or a function outside SQLite for T-status queries (lint test).

title: Stats store: append-only outcome, link, decision and feedback fact shapes
body:
## Goal
Create the append-only tables and writers for `fact_outcome`, `fact_link` and `fact_feedback` (shape only; D6 owns
the values), and the `fact_decision` projection of D5/D6's `decision_record`. Enforce append-only with a guard.
Supplement §5 outcome capture and §9 decision record: storage only.

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §4.2.1 (`fact_decision`, `fact_outcome`, `fact_feedback`, `fact_link`), §4.2.2 (closed outcome codes),
§4.2.3 (`tag_assignment` and label source). AD7: decisions and attempts are addressable events; feedback and
outcomes are append-only; nothing rewrites a record. R3 §4.2 (Langfuse scores pattern).

## Files
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/outcomes.mjs` (new): `appendOutcome`, `appendLink`, `appendFeedback`; no update or
  delete function exists.
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/outcomes.test.mjs` (new).
- `pm-stack/route-ledger-export/dims/outcome_codes.json` (new): the closed list with a definition per code.

## Approach
Writers only insert; `current` is a view. The outcome code list is loaded from the JSON; an unknown code is rejected.
`observed_by` ∈ {self, parent, reviewer, system, user}. The `decision_record` projection reads D5/D6's table when it
exists; until then the projection is an empty view with the columns in design §4.2.1.

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `bun test pm-stack/route-ledger-export/outcomes.test.mjs` passes.
2. Guard (exact): a test greps the module for `UPDATE`, `DELETE` and `DROP` statements and fails if any appears.
3. Property test: for any sequence of appended outcomes for one subject, `v_outcome_current` returns exactly the latest
   by `observed_at_ms` per `outcome_code` (generator-based).
4. Code list parity: the outcome codes in `outcome_codes.json` equal the enum in design §4.2.2 (exact set equality).

title: Stats store research: DeepSeek 1107 presence, AA crosswalk coverage, reasoning-token convention
body:
## Goal
Answer with data the three questions the store cannot answer from the ledger: (1) is `1107` a served DeepSeek variant
anywhere in the ledger, the config, or the provider docs, and which doors serve which variant; (2) what share of
ledger model ids have an AA price row after a reviewed crosswalk; (3) whether `tokens_output` includes reasoning tokens
(overlaps D3-S7; this slice gives the evidence for both).

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §2 fact 4 (no `1107` in 649,414 ledger rows), §7 Q-D3-1, Q-D3-3, Q-D3-13. Config files: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.jsonc`
and `.bak-*`; `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` in this repo. Provider docs via web search only (no credentials).

## Deliverable
`doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/research/R3b-variant-and-crosswalk.md` (new), with: the
ledger/config evidence paths, the variant-per-door table, the crosswalk coverage count, and a recommendation for
`dim_model_alias`. Every external claim carries a URL; unverified claims are marked **[unverified]**.

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `grep -c "1107" ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is not used (DB is binary); instead the report lists each
   query used with its result (the live query `select count(*) from route_attempt where model_id like '%1107%'`).
2. Crosswalk coverage: the report gives `n_matched / n_distinct_model_ids` for the last 30 days, computed by a script
   committed alongside it.
3. The report names the **RULING** items for Drew (Q-D3-1) with the default applied.

title: Stats store V3: measured tail bands and drift guard for D1 and D4 values
body:
## Goal
Per door and effort, a measured median, p90 and p99 band from `v_attempt` (with `n`), and a guard that fails when a
current measured value drifts beyond its recorded band. Feeds D1 overlay values with provenance `measured`.

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. 14 days of facts per tuned decision (main.md §0).

1. Guard test: for a fixture where one door's p90 moves beyond its band, the guard exits non-zero and names the door
   (exact).

title: Stats store guard: every quantile is printed with its n
body:
## Goal
A guard over every query output and every rollup row: a quantile value is never shown without `n`, and a quantile below
its threshold is marked `unresolved`. Enforces brief §5 "statistics wherever possible" with the honesty rule of design §4.4.

## Context
Design: `doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D3-stats-store.md` on main (section refs below). Program: code#9399, pool & effort system. Standing rules: gh CLI only; merge commits only; CI on main only; secrets by name only; read `opencode.db` read-only (`mode=ro`), never write it.
Design §4.4 reporting rules 1–4; §7 Q-D3-4 (thresholds p90 ≥ 100, p99.9 ≥ 1000 — defaults, heuristic). Oracle: the
prototype's note that every day cell at 20 seeds was below 1,000 (p99.9 unresolved).

## Files
- `scripts/stats/check_quantile_reporting.py` (new, stdlib): reads a result file (CSV/JSON) and fails when a column named
  `p90|p99|p999|median|q1|q3` lacks a sibling `n` column or an `unresolved` flag where `n` is below threshold.
- `scripts/stats/test_check_quantile_reporting.py` (new).

## Acceptance (runnable)
1. `python3 -I scripts/stats/test_check_quantile_reporting.py` passes (fixtures: a good file, a file missing `n`, a file with
   `p999` and `n = 500` lacking the flag; the checker must reject the last two).
2. Run against the Q15 output of D3-S10 on the live DB: exit 0 (every row carries `n`, rows with n < 1000 have p999 flagged).
